I've only seen aphids on a few weeds in my yard, almost never on a plant I eat. And they're normally gone in a week.

This past spring I had a plum tree with some branches and leaves covered in aphids. I just blasted them off with the water hose spray nozzle. Of course this didn't get rid of all of them, but definitely cut down on the infestation. It wasn't long after that the ladybugs showed up and I started seeing their eggs, and ultimately the larvae eradicated the remaining aphids.

I also used tanglefoot around the trunks of my two apple trees. It prevented the ants from getting to the aphids and protecting them or moving them around, and seems to have a good job of keeping them at bay. Of course not much use for it on your lettuce. You might try covering them with netting, as I've had success using that to protect young plants.
